passages.note: House third-reading Yea on 2SB 100; 6 Nays of a 75-member body is under 10%, so it cannot carry a chair alone.
passages.actor_quote: Ward, R. Whyte, S. Wilcox, R.

passages.provision_quote: (b) without written parental consent make changes to a student's education record
passages.note: Operative text guarantees parental access to education records and requires consent for gender-identity changes to the record, which rules out rungs 1-2 but matches neither 'tell parents when parents ask' nor 'permission before staff use a different name or pronouns' (its object is the record, not staff usage).

rows.reasoning: Whyte voted Yea on SB 100 (2023), which bars schools from shielding a student's education record from parents and bars, 'without written parental consent', changes to the record regarding gender identity. That shows the parental-disclosure side, but the vote is near-unanimous and the bill's object (the education record) does not match every clause of 'Require parental permission before staff use a different name or pronouns' or 'Require schools to tell parents when parents ask', so no rung is established.
